```{r setup, include=FALSE}
# 1. Knitr Options
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = here::here())

# 2. Load Packages
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(tidyverse)  # Loads dplyr, ggplot2, tidyr, readr, etc.
  library(here)
  library(fs)
  library(knitr)
  library(kableExtra)
  library(writexl)
  library(ggprism)
})

# 3. Define Absolute Paths
data_path <- here::here(params$data_dir, params$data_file)
out_dir   <- here::here(params$out_dir)
fig_dir   <- here::here(params$fig_dir)

# 4. Create Folders (fs::dir_create handles existence checks automatically)
fs::dir_create(c(out_dir, fig_dir))
```

# Read in the PANAS data
```{r, read-data, include =TRUE}
data_path <- file.path(params$data_dir, params$data_file)

# diagnostics 
cat("Working directory:", getwd(), "\n")
cat("Expecting data at:", data_path, "\n")
if (dir.exists(params$data_dir)) {
  cat("Files in", params$data_dir, ":\n"); print(list.files(params$data_dir, pattern = "\\.(csv|xlsx)$"))
} else {
  cat("Directory", params$data_dir, "does not exist relative to getwd().\n")
}

if (!file.exists(data_path)) stop("Data file not found: ", data_path)

raw_panas <- read_csv(data_path, show_col_types = FALSE)
cat("Read data: rows =", nrow(raw_panas), "cols =", ncol(raw_panas), "\n")


```

# Clean the PANAS data
```{r, data-cleaning}
# Create week_label, week, time_of_day, valence and week_group (BSL -> Baseline; SRT weeks 1-4)
panas <- raw_panas %>%
  mutate(
    week_label = case_when(
      day >= 1 & day <= 7 & timepoint == "BSL" ~ "BSL",
      day >= 8 & day <= 14 & timepoint == "BSL" ~ "BSL",
      day >= 1 & day <= 7 & timepoint == "SRT" ~ "1",
      day >= 8 & day <= 14 & timepoint == "SRT" ~ "2",
      day >= 15 & day <= 21 & timepoint == "SRT" ~ "3",
      day >= 22 & day <= 28 & timepoint == "SRT" ~ "4",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    week = cut(
      day,
      breaks = seq(0, max(day, na.rm = TRUE), by = 7),
      labels = paste0("Week", seq_len(length(seq(0, max(day, na.rm = TRUE), by = 7)) - 1)),
      include.lowest = TRUE
    ),
    time_of_day = factor(time_of_day, levels = c("morning","evening"),
                         labels = c("Morning","Evening")),
    valence = factor(valence, levels = c("positive","negative"),
                     labels = c("Positive","Negative"))
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    week_group = case_when(
      timepoint == "BSL" & week_label == "BSL" ~ "Baseline",
      TRUE ~ as.character(week_label)
    ),
    week_group = factor(week_group, levels = c("Baseline","1","2","3","4"))
  )

# Save cleaned snapshot
write_xlsx(panas, path = file.path(params$clean_dir, "panas_data_clean.xlsx"))

cat("panas rows:", nrow(panas), "unique Record ID:", n_distinct(panas$`Record ID`), "\n")
print(names(panas))

```

#  Calculate time gap between PANAS completion and bedtime/risetime
```{r}

library(tidyverse)
library(lubridate)
library(hms)

# 1. Load the processed Diary data
# This ensures diary_final is available in your PANAS script
diary_path <- here::here("Data", "processed", "sleep_diary", "diary_data_clean.csv")

if (!file.exists(diary_path)) {
  stop("Processed diary file not found! Run the Sleep Diary script first.")
}

diary_final <- read_csv(diary_path, show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  mutate(
    # Essential: Ensure ID is padded and Date is a Date object for the join
    Id = str_pad(as.character(Id), width = 3, side = "left", pad = "0"),
    Date = as.Date(Date)
  )

# 1. Standardize PANAS Data (Both Morning and Evening)
panas_standardized <- raw_panas %>%
  mutate(
    Id = str_pad(as.character(`Record ID`), width = 3, side = "left", pad = "0"),
    panas_comp_dt = dmy_hm(clock_time_completed),
    match_date = as.Date(panas_comp_dt),
    time_of_day = tolower(time_of_day)
  ) %>%
  distinct(Id, match_date, time_of_day, .keep_all = TRUE)

# 2. Join with Diary Data
adherence_joined <- panas_standardized %>%
  inner_join(diary_final, by = c("Id", "match_date" = "Date")) %>%
  mutate(
    # Gap calculation based on time of day
    gap_mins = case_when(
      time_of_day == "evening" ~ as.numeric(difftime(bed_datetime, panas_comp_dt, units = "mins")),
      time_of_day == "morning" ~ as.numeric(difftime(panas_comp_dt, rise_datetime, units = "mins")),
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    )
  ) %>%
  # Filter out negatives (completed after bed or before rising)
  filter(!is.na(gap_mins), gap_mins >= 0)

# 3. Final Summary Table
adherence_summary <- adherence_joined %>%
  group_by(time_of_day) %>%
  summarise(
    avg_gap_mins = mean(gap_mins, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_gap_mins  = sd(gap_mins, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_obs        = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    # Format for easy reading in the report
    avg_hhmm = as_hms(round(avg_gap_mins * 60)),
    sd_hhmm  = as_hms(round(sd_gap_mins * 60))
  )

# 4. Display results clearly
knitr::kable(adherence_summary, 
             caption = "Time Gap between PANAS Completion and Sleep Diary Timestamps",
             col.names = c("Session", "Avg Mins", "SD Mins", "N", "Avg (HH:MM)", "SD (HH:MM)"))


library(tidyverse)
library(hms)

panas_circular_stats <- panas_standardized %>%
  mutate(
    # 1. Convert completion time to decimal hours
    comp_hour_dec = hour(panas_comp_dt) + (minute(panas_comp_dt) / 60),
    # 2. Convert hours to Radians (0-24 -> 0-2pi)
    angle_rad = (comp_hour_dec / 24) * 2 * pi
  ) %>%
  group_by(time_of_day) %>%
  summarise(
    n_obs = n(),
    mean_sin = mean(sin(angle_rad), na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_cos = mean(cos(angle_rad), na.rm = TRUE),
    # R is the mean resultant length (0 to 1). 
    # Closer to 1 means the times are very tightly clustered.
    R = sqrt(mean_sin^2 + mean_cos^2),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    # 3. Calculate Mean Angle and convert back to 24h decimal
    avg_rad = atan2(mean_sin, mean_cos),
    avg_hour_dec = (avg_rad * 24) / (2 * pi),
    avg_hour_dec = ifelse(avg_hour_dec < 0, avg_hour_dec + 24, avg_hour_dec),
    
    # 4. Calculate Circular Standard Deviation
    # Formula: sqrt(-2 * log(R)) in radians, then converted to hours
    sd_rad = sqrt(-2 * log(R)),
    sd_hour_dec = (sd_rad * 24) / (2 * pi),
    
    # 5. Format as readable HMS
    avg_clock_time = as_hms(round(avg_hour_dec * 3600)),
    sd_clock_time  = as_hms(round(sd_hour_dec * 3600))
  )

# Display the results
knitr::kable(panas_circular_stats %>% 
               select(time_of_day, n_obs, avg_clock_time, sd_clock_time), 
             caption = "Circular Mean and SD of PANAS Completion Times",
             col.names = c("Session", "N", "Mean Clock Time", "Circular SD"))
```

# Plot weekly PANAS scores
```{r}
## Plot weekly PANAS scores
# prepare plotting summary with SE and enforce x-axis order
panas_plot_week <- panas %>% # Changed from raw_panas to panas
  mutate(
    # Ensure week_clean is based on the already created week_label
    week_clean = factor(week_label, levels = c("BSL", "1", "2", "3", "4"))
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(week_clean)) %>%
  group_by(valence, time_of_day, week_clean) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_score = mean(score, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_score = sd(score, na.rm = TRUE),
    n = sum(!is.na(score)),
    se_score = sd_score / sqrt(pmax(n, 1)),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Define colors
cols <- c("Positive" = "#00968a", "Negative" = "#c81f6e")

# 4. Create the Plot
p <- ggplot(panas_plot_week, aes(x = week_clean, y = mean_score, group = valence)) +
  # Background shading for Evening facet
  geom_rect(data = subset(panas_plot_week, time_of_day == "Evening"),
            aes(xmin = -Inf, xmax = Inf, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf),
            fill = "grey95", inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  geom_line(aes(color = valence), linewidth = 1) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = mean_score - se_score, ymax = mean_score + se_score, color = valence),
                width = 0.2, linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(aes(fill = valence, color = valence), shape = 16, size = 4) +
  facet_wrap(~ time_of_day, nrow = 1) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = cols) +
  scale_color_manual(values = cols) +
  # Adjusted limits to 30 to ensure error bars aren't cut off if data is high
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(10, 25), breaks = seq(10, 50, 5), expand = c(0,0)) +
  labs(x = "Study Week", y = "PANAS Score", fill = "Valence", color = "Valence") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    axis.line = element_line(colour = "black", linewidth = 0.8),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"), 
    axis.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    legend.position = "top"
  )

print(p)

# 5. Save plot to files (Figure 3)
ggsave(
  filename = file.path(fig_dir, "Figure 3.tif"), 
  plot = p, 
  width = 6, 
  height = 4.5, 
  dpi = 300,
  compression = "lzw" 
)

```

# Plot across each day of the 1st week of SRT 
```{r}
# 1. Prepare Daily Plotting Summary
panas_plot_daily <- panas %>%
  mutate(
    # Create the specific labels
    day_label = case_when(
      timepoint == "BSL" ~ "Baseline",
      day == 28 | timepoint == "FU" ~ "Follow-up",
      day >= 1 & day <= 7 ~ paste0("Day", day),
      TRUE ~ NA_character_ # Filters out any other days
    ),
    # Set the levels to control the order on the X-axis
    day_label = factor(day_label, levels = c(
      "Baseline", 
      paste0("Day", 1:7), 
      "Follow-up"
    )),
    time_of_day = factor(time_of_day, levels = c("Morning", "Evening")),
    valence = factor(valence, levels = c("Negative", "Positive"))
  ) %>%
  # Remove the NAs (days between 7 and 28)
  filter(!is.na(day_label), !is.na(score)) %>%
  group_by(valence, time_of_day, day_label) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_score = mean(score, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_score = sd(score, na.rm = TRUE),
    n = n(),
    se_score = sd_score / sqrt(pmax(n, 1)),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# 2. Colors & Plotting
cols <- c("Positive" = "#00968a", "Negative" = "#c81f6e")

p_daily <- ggplot(panas_plot_daily, aes(x = day_label, y = mean_score, color = valence, group = valence)) +
  # Add Grey Background to Evening
  geom_rect(data = subset(panas_plot_daily, time_of_day == "Evening"),
            aes(xmin = -Inf, xmax = Inf, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf),
            fill = "grey90", inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  
  # Error bars, Lines, and Points
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = mean_score - se_score, ymax = mean_score + se_score), 
                width = 0.2, linewidth = 1) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  # Using shape 21 for the black outline effect seen in your image
  geom_point(size = 4, aes(fill = valence), shape = 21, color = "black", stroke = 0.5) +
  
  # Faceting
  facet_wrap(~ time_of_day, nrow = 1) +
  
  # Scales & Formatting
  scale_color_manual(values = cols) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = cols) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(10, 25), breaks = seq(10, 25, 5)) +
  
  # Labels and Theme
  labs(x = NULL, y = "PANAS Score") +
  theme_bw() + 
  theme(
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    panel.border = element_blank(),
    axis.line = element_line(color = "black", linewidth = 1),
    strip.background = element_blank(),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12),
    legend.position = "top",
    legend.title = element_blank(),
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, vjust = 1, hjust = 1, color = "black", face = "bold"),
    axis.text.y = element_text(color = "black", face = "bold"),
    axis.title.y = element_text(face = "bold")
  )

# 3. Save as Figure S2
ggsave(file.path(fig_dir, "Figure S2.jpg"), p_daily, width = 10, height = 7, dpi = 600)

print(p_daily)
```

# Linear Mixed Model
```{r}
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(lme4)
  library(emmeans)
  library(writexl)
})

# Prepare phase_week variable (Baseline, Week1..Week4)
panas_data_week <- panas %>%
  mutate(
    phase_week = case_when(
      timepoint == "BSL" ~ "Baseline",
      timepoint == "SRT" & week_group %in% c("1","2","3","4") ~ paste0("Week", week_group),
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    phase_week = factor(phase_week, levels = c("Baseline", paste0("Week",1:4)))
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(phase_week))

# ensure ordering for final table
panas_data_week$valence <- factor(panas_data_week$valence, 
                                  levels = c("Positive", "Negative"))
panas_data_week$time_of_day <- factor(panas_data_week$time_of_day, 
                                      levels = c("Morning", "Evening"))

# safe LMM runner: returns data.frame of contrasts or NULL
run_lmm_by_week <- function(data_subset) {
  data_subset <- data_subset %>% filter(!is.na(score))
  if (n_distinct(data_subset$`Record ID`) < 2) return(NULL)
  fit <- tryCatch(lmer(score ~ phase_week + (1 | `Record ID`), 
                       data = data_subset, REML = TRUE),
                  error = function(e) return(NULL))
  if (is.null(fit)) return(NULL)
  emms <- tryCatch(emmeans(fit, specs = "phase_week"), error = function(e) return(NULL))
  if (is.null(emms)) return(NULL)
  contr <- tryCatch(contrast(emms, method = "trt.vs.ctrl", ref = "Baseline") %>% 
                      summary(infer = TRUE, adjust = "none"),
                    error = function(e) return(NULL))
  if (is.null(contr)) return(NULL)
  sd_resid <- sigma(fit)
  out <- as.data.frame(contr) %>%
    mutate(
      Cohens_d = estimate / sd_resid
    )
  return(out)
}

# loop across valence × time_of_day and collect results
results_list <- list()
for (v in levels(panas_data_week$valence)) {
  for (t in levels(panas_data_week$time_of_day)) {
    subset_data <- filter(panas_data_week, valence == v, time_of_day == t)
    if (nrow(subset_data) > 0) {
      res <- run_lmm_by_week(subset_data)
      if (!is.null(res)) {
        res$valence <- v
        res$time_of_day <- t
        results_list[[paste(v, t, sep = "_")]] <- res
      }
    }
  }
}

# combine, format, order (Positive first, Morning first), drop p-value column
if (length(results_list) > 0) {
  panas_lmm_results_by_week <- bind_rows(results_list) %>%
    # numeric columns (keep numeric estimate for downstream use)
    mutate(
      estimate = as.numeric(estimate),
      lower.CL = as.numeric(lower.CL),
      upper.CL = as.numeric(upper.CL),
      CI_range = paste0(sprintf("%.2f", lower.CL), " to ", sprintf("%.2f", upper.CL)),
      Cohens_d = round(as.numeric(Cohens_d), 2)
    ) %>%
    # enforce ordering columns and rows: Positive first, Morning first
    mutate(
      valence = factor(valence, levels = c("Positive", "Negative")),
      time_of_day = factor(time_of_day, levels = c("Morning", "Evening"))
    ) %>%
    arrange(valence, time_of_day, contrast) %>%
    select(valence, time_of_day, contrast, estimate, lower.CL, upper.CL, CI_range, Cohens_d)



  # Print a clean table for the report (format numbers, no p-value)
  panas_lmm_results_by_week %>%
    mutate(
      Estimate = sprintf("%.2f", estimate),
      `Lower 95%` = sprintf("%.2f", lower.CL),
      `Upper 95%` = sprintf("%.2f", upper.CL),
      `95% CI` = CI_range,
      `Cohen's d` = sprintf("%.2f", Cohens_d)
    ) %>%
    select(valence, time_of_day, contrast, Estimate, `95% CI`, `Cohen's d`) %>%
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, 
               caption = "LMM contrasts vs Baseline (adjusted difference and 95% CI)",
               escape = TRUE)

} else {
  cat("No LMM results produced (check data / grouping).")
}

# Create and Save Professional Word Table

library(flextable)
library(officer)

if (exists("panas_lmm_results_by_week") && nrow(panas_lmm_results_by_week) > 0) {
  
  # 1. Prepare data for flextable
  table_df <- panas_lmm_results_by_week %>%
    mutate(
      estimate = sprintf("%.2f", estimate),
      Cohens_d = sprintf("%.2f", Cohens_d)
    ) %>%
    select(valence, time_of_day, contrast, estimate, CI_range, Cohens_d) %>%
    rename(
      `Valence` = valence,
      `Time of Day` = time_of_day,
      `Contrast` = contrast,
      `Estimate` = estimate,
      `95% CI` = CI_range,
      `Cohen's d` = Cohens_d
    )

  # 2. Build the flextable
  ft <- flextable(table_df) %>%
    # Merge vertical cells for cleaner look
    merge_v(j = c("Valence", "Time of Day")) %>% 
    # Formatting
    theme_booktabs() %>% 
    autofit() %>%
    bold(part = "header") %>%
    align(j = 4:6, align = "center", part = "all") %>%
    set_caption("Linear Mixed Model: Contrasts vs Baseline for PANAS Scores") %>%
    # Fix border lines after merging
    fix_border_issues()

  # 3. Save as Word Doc
  save_as_docx(ft, path = file.path(out_dir, "PANAS_LMM_Results_Table.docx"))
  
  # Preview in the report
  ft
} else {
  message("No results available to export.")
}

```
